\begin{Theorem}[{see Proposition~\ref{prop_preserve_consistent1} and Theorem~\ref{mutation=deformation1} for more details}]\label{thm_main_intro}
In addition to the above settings, we also assume that either one of the following conditions is satisfied:
\begin{itemize}\itemsep=0pt
\item[$(i)$] $r=1$ or
\item[$(ii)$] $\Gamma$ is a hexagonal or rectangular dimer model $($see Definition~{\rm \ref{def_hexagonal_square})}.
\end{itemize}
Then the deformations $\nu_\bfp^\zig(\Gamma,\{z_1,\dots,z_r\})$ and $\nu_\bfp^\zag(\Gamma,\{z_1,\dots,z_r\})$ are consistent dimer models,
and we have
\begin{gather*}\mutation_{w}(\Delta_\Gamma,F)=\Delta_{\nu^\zig_\bfp(\Gamma,\{z_1,\dots,z_r\})},\qquad
\mutation_{w}(\Delta_\Gamma,-F)=\Delta_{\nu^\zag_\bfp(\Gamma,\{z_1,\dots,z_r\})},
\end{gather*}
where $\Delta_{\nu^\zig_\bfp(\Gamma,\{z_1,\dots,z_r\})}$ and $\Delta_{\nu^\zag_\bfp(\Gamma,\{z_1,\dots,z_r\})}$ are the perfect matching polygons of
$\nu_\bfp^\zig(\Gamma,\{z_1,\dots,\allowbreak z_r\})$ and $\nu_\bfp^\zag(\Gamma,\{z_1,\dots,z_r\})$, respectively.
\end{Theorem}
